subject: physics

concepts.title: Light Velocity in Optical Medium
concepts.definition: The phase velocity of an electromagnetic wave in a dense optical medium is calculated by dividing the speed of light in vacuum by the medium refractive index.
concepts.key_idea: Speed of light decreases proportionally to the refractive index when propagating through matter.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics find the speed of light in glass given refractive index
calculate the velocity of light in a liquid with known refractive index
what is the speed of light wave in medium with refractive index n
determine light propagation speed inside a transparent medium
compute the speed of light in water given its refractive index

solution_steps.action: divide vacuum speed of light by refractive index
solution_steps.explain: refractive index is the ratio of speed of light in vacuum to speed in medium

concepts.title: Wavelength Alteration in Refracted Waves
concepts.definition: When light refracts into a medium of higher refractive index, its spatial wavelength shortens while its temporal frequency remains unchanged.
concepts.key_idea: Light wavelength scales inversely with the refractive index of the medium.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics calculate the wavelength of light in water
find the reduced wavelength of monochromatic light in glass
determine the light wavelength inside a medium with refractive index n
what is the wavelength of light after entering a denser medium
compute wavelength of refracted ray in medium of refractive index

solution_steps.action: divide vacuum wavelength by refractive index
solution_steps.explain: frequency remains constant during refraction so wavelength decreases by factor of n

concepts.title: Critical Angle for Total Internal Reflection
concepts.definition: The sine of the critical angle of incidence is equal to the ratio of the refractive index of the rarer medium to that of the denser medium.
concepts.key_idea: At angles of incidence beyond the critical angle light undergoes total internal reflection.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics calculate sine of critical angle for interface
find sin of critical angle between glass and air
determine the sine value of critical angle for water glass boundary
what is the sine of critical angle when light travels from dense to rare medium
compute sin of critical angle for total internal reflection

solution_steps.action: divide rarer refractive index by denser refractive index
solution_steps.explain: sine of critical angle equals ratio of refractive indices n2 over n1

concepts.title: Interference Resultant Intensity
concepts.definition: The net intensity produced by two coherent sources of equal amplitude varies as four times individual source intensity multiplied by cosine squared of half phase difference.
concepts.key_idea: Superposition produces constructive intensity up to four times single source intensity.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics find resultant intensity for phase difference
calculate interference light intensity given individual intensity and cos squared half phase
determine resultant intensity at a point on screen in double slit interference
what is the net intensity when two coherent light waves interfere
compute interference intensity for given phase angle component

solution_steps.action: multiply four times source intensity by square of cosine of half phase angle
solution_steps.explain: interference formula gives I = 4 * I0 * cos^2(phase/2)

concepts.title: Bright Fringe Position in Young Double Slit
concepts.definition: The distance from central bright maximum to the nth bright fringe on an observation screen equals n times wavelength times screen distance divided by slit separation.
concepts.key_idea: Bright fringe positions scale linearly with order number, wavelength, and distance to screen.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics calculate the position of nth bright fringe
find distance of fourth bright fringe from central maximum
determine bright fringe location in Young double slit experiment
what is the position of bright fringe on screen given wavelength and geometry
compute distance of bright fringe in interference pattern

solution_steps.action: multiply fringe order by wavelength and screen distance
solution_steps.explain: calculate path difference condition product for bright fringe
divide numerator by distance between the two slits

concepts.title: Interference Fringe Width
concepts.definition: The constant spatial distance separating adjacent bright or dark interference fringes on a screen in Young double slit setup.
concepts.key_idea: Fringe width is directly proportional to wavelength and screen distance, and inversely proportional to slit distance.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics calculate the fringe width in Young double slit experiment
find fringe spacing given wavelength screen distance and slit separation
determine distance between consecutive bright fringes on screen
what is the fringe width of interference pattern
compute fringe width in double slit setup

solution_steps.explain: product of wavelength and screen separation distance
fringe width beta equals lambda D over d

concepts.title: Single Slit Diffraction Minimum Angle
concepts.definition: The sine of angular position for nth diffraction minimum produced by a single slit equals n times wavelength divided by slit width.
concepts.key_idea: Diffraction minima occur where secondary wavelets from opposite halves of the slit destructively interfere.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics find sine of diffraction angle for first minimum
calculate sin theta for single slit diffraction minimum
determine sine of angular direction of nth dark fringe in diffraction
what is sin theta for diffraction minimum with given slit width
compute sine of angle of diffraction dark band

solution_steps.action: multiply order by wavelength and divide by slit width
solution_steps.explain: sin theta equals n times lambda divided by slit width a

concepts.title: Polarized Light Transmission and Malus Law
concepts.definition: According to Malus law the transmitted intensity of linearly polarized light through an analyzer equals initial intensity times cosine squared of angle between transmission axes.
concepts.key_idea: Intensity of transmitted polarized wave varies with the square of cosine of transmission angle.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics calculate transmitted intensity using Malus law
find light intensity after passing through secondary polaroid
determine transmitted intensity given initial polarized intensity and cosine squared angle
what is the final light intensity emerging from analyzer polaroid
compute light intensity after polaroid filter using Malus law

solution_steps.action: multiply initial polarized intensity by square of cosine of orientation angle
solution_steps.explain: Malus law relates transmitted intensity to cosine square of axis angle

concepts.title: Wavefront Propagation Distance
concepts.definition: The outward spatial distance traveled by a wavefront during time interval t is equal to wave propagation velocity multiplied by time.
concepts.key_idea: Wavefronts expand as secondary wavelets propagate outward at wave speed.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics calculate wavefront distance traveled in given time
find distance secondary wavelets travel in time interval
determine radius of spherical secondary wavelet after time t
what distance does a light wavefront advance in medium
compute displacement of wavefront during time duration

solution_steps.action: multiply wave speed by time interval
solution_steps.explain: distance equals velocity times time according to Huygens wavelet expansion

concepts.title: Wavefront Transformation by Lenses and Mirrors
concepts.definition: Refraction or reflection by optical elements reshapes incident plane wavefronts into spherical or tilted surfaces while preserving equal travel time across all rays.
concepts.key_idea: The total travel time from object to image is identical along all ray paths.
question_patterns: in Class 12 Wave Optics explain how plane wavefront changes on passing through convex lens
describe wavefront transformation after reflection from concave mirror
why is travel time along all rays equal when real image is formed by convex lens
what shape does plane wavefront take after traversing thin glass prism
explain wavefront distortion during refraction through converging optical element

solution_steps.explain: different parts of wavefront experience different thickness of medium, delaying central or peripheral portions
emerging wavefront bends into spherical shape converging toward focal point or tilts depending on element shape
